content.thinking:
I'm checking each claim against the source. The statement about shoppers being unable to open their account pages is supported as a description of what readers saw and the cause. The admin's monthly spending summary and its division-by-zero failure also check out, as does the likely impact on repeat buyers with no purchases yet this month. The estimate of lost takings is supported too, and I'm now starting on the claim about when the outage happened.

I'm working through the rest of the claims, which all check out against the source: the cost of the responders' time, the decision to switch the new feature back off and the fact that it is still off, and the code fix that has only been proposed and not applied.

content.text: All seven claims in the overview are supported by the record, and I found nothing to flag. The overview has no went_wrong field, so that check didn't apply.

supported.quote: For {duration}, some shoppers on io-shop could not open their account pages.
rows: What a reader saw: Shoppers' account pages failed to load

supported.quote: An admin had switched on a new monthly spending summary for those pages, and its calculation failed with a division by zero.
This most likely hit shoppers who had bought before but had bought nothing yet this month.
Argus estimates the shop lost {customer_loss} in takings.
rows: What it cost the shop in takings (estimated by Argus): 5,194.52 USD {customer_loss}

supported.quote: The time of the people who responded cost {responder_cost}.
Argus ended the incident by turning the new feature back off, and it is still off.
rows: Argus: reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature - confirmed, still in place

supported.quote: Argus has also proposed a code fix, but it is only a draft and has not been applied.
rows: Argus: proposed a fix, PR #579 - opened as a draft
